title: Support a group while refusing one misleading claim

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Loyalty can protect a group’s legitimate purpose by correcting a misleading claim. Replacing one unsupported boast with another is still misleading; truthful alternatives need their own evidence.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Club record:24 seats were offered,18 attended, and the event took place as scheduled. No satisfaction survey, discussion-quality observation or photograph permission exists. Draft: “Our fully attended event inspired everyone.” The editor invites factual corrections; you support the club’s continuing work.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Write a respectful objection and a publishable factual alternative. Identify both claims that lack support and one constructive way to learn about reception later.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A teammate says accuracy will make the club look less successful. Does that establish a legitimate duty to retain the false number?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: “The event took place as scheduled, with 18 attendees” is supported. Full attendance and universal inspiration are not. Asking willing participants for optional feedback later could inform a narrower attributed statement, but has not occurred. Partial: fix full attendance while leaving “inspired everyone.” Incorrect: substitute “strong discussion” without evidence or allege dishonest motives.
criteria: The objection addresses conduct not invented motive
Legitimate loyalty is separated from complicity

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Serve the shared purpose with accurate reporting and an appropriate correction process. An unwanted accurate figure is not disloyal merely because it is less flattering.
